title: Customer ad-hoc quantization exemption and manual calibration for FP8/INT8 model
creator: Maya Chen
description: Customer 'AtlasEdge' requested an exception to bypass the default FP8 automatic rejection policy after running the self-serve quantization flow. Their proprietary transformer variant shows >1.5% BLEU/perplexity degradation under the standard FP8 profile. They asked for a supported, engineer-run manual calibration that uses per-channel clipping, extended KL search, and bespoke outlier handling so they can validate FP8 in production. Ticket came in via Support (Anna Patel) and includes a request to produce an exportable quantization profile and a reproducible calibration artifact that we can pin in runtime for the customer. This ticket coordinates Solutions Eng, Runtime, and the Calibration team to run a set of manual calibration experiments, log full distribution histograms, and run the customer's eval suite to quantify delta relative to FP32. We must also validate a fallback policy (INT8 or FP32) and document guardrails for future exceptions.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Provide a reproducible calibration artifact (.qprof) that the customer can pin in runtime
A2: Measured end-to-end accuracy delta on customer eval suite <= 1.0% relative to FP32 (primary metric: perplexity for LM; secondary: task-specific BLEU/EM)
A3: Throughput and latency remain within 1.2x of dedicated INT8 baseline or documented with trade-offs
A4: PR with runtime change to allow pinning profile + config flag reviewed and merged
A5: Knowledge doc and runbook created in Confluence for future similar exceptions
updates: 2026-02-11 - Triaged by Maya; assigned to Rafael. Support provided initial repro artifacts and a trimmed eval set.

2026-02-15 - Preliminary profiling: observed large dynamic range in attention projection weights and several outlier tokens. Suggested per-channel clipping and increasing KL search bins. Rafael flagged potential GPU kernel mismatch for FP8 path.

2026-02-20 - Manual calibration run 1 completed (cbr-20260220-01). Top-1 perplexity delta -1.7% (worse). Decided to change outlier handling to percentile-based clipping and re-run with extended sampling.

2026-02-27 - Calibration run 2 (cbr-20260227-02) used percentile clipping at 99.995 and per-channel scale. Perplexity delta improved to -0.9%. Eng reviews indicate this is near threshold but toolchain needs a reproducible profile file.

2026-03-01 - Security and infra reviewed storage/transfer of .qprof artifact. Solutions Eng approved customer export with HMAC-signed artifact. Support confirmed customer can consume pinned profile via Dedicated API.
2026-03-06 - Created PR #1489 to allow runtime pinning of external quant profiles; small API surface change and guardrails added. Requesting runtime engineering review.
2026-03-09 - Runtime review feedback: add validation check for model hash and enforce signed profile; Rafael updated PR to include validation and added telemetry event.

2026-03-12 - Validation run (cbr-20260311-03) executed against full eval set. Results logged and attached. Preparing runbook and customer handoff documentation. SLA change requested by Account team pending.

Notes: Customer asked for FP8 to stay in production if <=1% delta. If delta exceeds threshold, auto-fallback to INT8 is required. We agreed to one-time exception for pinning profile and to document process for future requests.
validation_results: cbr-20260220-01: baseline vs FP8 -> perplexity delta +1.7% (regression)
cbr-20260227-02: after percentile clipping -> perplexity delta +0.9% (within customer threshold)
cbr-20260311-03: full eval -> perplexity delta +0.6%; BLEU delta -0.4 points; latency change +18% at 1k token length
decision: Approve one-off FP8 exception with pinned .qprof export. Production deployment requires signed profile, model-hash validation, and auto-fallback to INT8 when live telemetry shows accuracy drift >1.5% over a rolling 24h window. Customer gets exported artifact and a runbook. Runtime change merged in PR #1489 and scheduled for runtime-1.22 rollout behind a feature flag.
